catalog_name: GitHub CSS research for static GitHub Pages websites

research_scope.coverage: Curated shortlist from topic discovery and direct GitHub repository reads; not exhaustive

research_methodology.primary_evidence: GitHub repository API metadata through GitHub connector, repository README/package files and GitHub CSS topic index.
research_methodology.date_field_definition: last_code_push_utc is GitHub pushed_at, not last page update or release date.
evaluation_limitations: GitHub pushed_at may reflect automated commits
No independent browser compatibility tests run
No production file size measurements conducted except publisher claim
No security audit or npm vulnerability scan performed
Authoring scores and advice are editorial assessment, not measurements
Unknown or unverified values are null

scoring_model.score: 20 × weighted average of six editorial criteria; higher ranks are better
scoring_model.ranking_note: Conditional resources may score well as libraries but are not default deployment recommendations.

recommended_css_technology_stack.intent: Responsive, accessible, fast static website with semantic HTML, vanilla JavaScript and no mandatory site build step.

core.purpose: Responsive CSS grid, baseline, form/table/menu modules
core.integration: Use only selected CSS modules; baseline includes Normalize.css.

core.purpose: Design tokens for colors, spacing, shadows, easing and optional motion
core.integration: Import selected prebuilt token modules, avoiding its normalize stylesheet.
Copy a font-family stack into custom CSS.
Vendor only chosen SVG assets; no runtime icon package.

recommended_css_technology_stack.author_css: A small site-specific stylesheet using CSS custom properties, Grid, Flexbox, media queries, focus-visible states and reduced-motion controls.

quality_assurance.purpose: Audit shipped pages; manually verify accessibility

optional_alternatives.when: Larger component library and richer built-in visual styling needed.
Generated utility CSS and a build process are acceptable.

do_not_combine: Multiple global CSS frameworks on the same page without strict scoping.
Pure baseline plus modern-normalize, sanitize.css or Open Props normalize unless intentionally overridden.
Tailwind preflight plus competing global reset styles.
Full alternative palette systems without a token naming strategy.
recommended_css_technology_stack.javascript_policy: No mandatory runtime JavaScript for styling; add targeted vanilla JavaScript only for behaviors such as navigation toggles, form validation or optional interactive components.
recommended_css_technology_stack.deployment_policy: For GitHub Pages, publish static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, font and SVG files; when using build-dependent CSS, compile first and publish resulting static artifacts.

prioritized_implementation_resources.reason: Select responsive grid and necessary components without a build pipeline.
Standardize design tokens; import only required variable sets.
Use system typography to avoid extra font requests.
Catch CSS errors with configured linting in development.
Measure and audit actual deployed pages.
Review keyboard usage, responsiveness, contrast, SEO and semantics.

integration_matrix.notes: Modular prebuilt CSS plus site-authored overrides; import only token modules and selected SVGs.
Remove duplicate or unneeded baseline styles in starter.
Pure incorporates Normalize.css; use one CSS normalization base.
Competing element defaults and baseline forms; avoid stacking.
Global component classes/reset conflicts and CSS bloat.
DaisyUI is Tailwind-dependent; pin matching versions and generate CSS before deploy.
Global baseline and utility class collisions can increase CSS size and specificity complexity.
Use explicit variable naming and test actual contrast pairings.
Use Prism theme CSS plus runtime highlighter JavaScript only when code blocks require syntax highlighting.

checks_to_perform: Keyboard-only navigation and visible focus state
Accessible names, ARIA usage where needed and semantic landmarks
Screen-reader review of menus and dialogs
Cross-browser stable Chrome, Firefox, Safari and mobile browsers
Lighthouse lab and field measurements as available
No duplicate CSS resets or CSS framework bundles
Self-host pinned SVG/font assets where appropriate and verify fonts licensing
preferred_patterns: Use semantic HTML and native controls before scripting.
Use :focus-visible, CSS Grid/Flexbox and min/max/clamp for responsive layout.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion and use animations only for meaningful affordances.
Minimize CSS shipped by selecting small modules and remove unused classes.
Test actual page, not only framework examples.

categories.description: Core CSS systems for layout, responsive design and components.
Composable variables, themes, palettes and design styling; prefer native CSS motion.
Ready-made motion effects; license and reduced-motion requirements apply.
System fonts, self-hosted font assets and font distribution.
Reusable SVG icons suitable for static HTML.
Build-time validation and documentation resources; not shipped to the site.
Integration helpers for HTML, documentation and specialized use cases.
